findings.claim: Across the full observed score window [0.0,0.49], the read landmark-00 and landmark-10 displacement and soft-mass curves are non-monotone: each shows multiple sign changes (4-10) and several strong sign conflicts (1-13) across 14 independent batches, so no single whole-window direction is established for these coordinates.

For the read curves, early-window and late-window rates have opposite signs (e.g. landmark_00_local_dx first_rate_z=-17.49 vs last_rate_z=+8.11; landmark_00_local_dy -72.37 vs +5.52; landmark_10_local_dx -42.98 vs +11.39; landmark_10_soft_mass +66.28 vs -11.56), indicating the local trend reverses within the window rather than a stationary target.

Whole-window mean z is small relative to the within-window excursions for every read curve (|whole_window_z| <= 0.64), and no read curve has polynomial_accepted=true (relative_node_RMSE 0.29-0.83), so a single global coordinate target is not supported by these observations.

hypotheses.direction: weaker control near the early negative excursion, stronger near the mid-window positive excursion, then weaker again late
hypotheses.falsifier: If a dose schedule that is flat across the window produces the same or better primary affinity than a schedule matching this mid-window emphasis, the timing hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.scope: regional (single landmark coordinate) over observed score nodes [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_dx coordinate shows a mid-window positive excursion (values_z rising to about +0.85 near t~0.10-0.11) bracketed by negative excursions early (t~0.15-0.19) and late (t~0.29-0.37), with the local rate flipping sign between the first and last nodes; a time-varying rather than constant control on this coordinate is worth testing.

hypotheses.direction: weaker control early, stronger control late
hypotheses.falsifier: If reversing the early/late dose ordering yields no measurable difference in the primary affinity metric, the timing contrast is not supported.
hypotheses.scope: regional (single landmark coordinate) over observed score nodes [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_dy coordinate is predominantly negative early (values_z down to about -1.26 near t~0.05) and rises toward near-zero/positive late (last_z ~ +0.13), with first_rate_z=-72.4 and last_rate_z=+5.5; this early-to-late sign reversal is a candidate timing contrast rather than a fixed target.

hypotheses.direction: stronger control mid-window, weaker at both ends
hypotheses.falsifier: If a mid-window-emphasized dose schedule does not change the primary affinity metric relative to a flat schedule, the occupancy-timing hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_10_soft_mass (soft occupancy mass at landmark 10, z-scored)
hypotheses.scope: regional (single landmark occupancy) over observed score nodes [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_10_soft_mass curve rises from negative early (first_z ~ -0.38) to a positive plateau (values_z ~ +0.7 to +1.0 across t~0.14-0.25) then declines late (last_z ~ -0.37), with first_rate_z=+66.3 and last_rate_z=-11.6; this is a mid-window occupancy emphasis candidate.

limitations: Only 8 of 200 catalogue curve features were read (landmark_00 and landmark_10 dx/dy/dz/soft_mass); the remaining 192 features are unqueried, not absent.
No stage or temporal profiles are available; only continuous curves were used.
All read curves are non-monotone with multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches; per-batch and clone-dependence structure was not resolved here.
Selection preference and coordinate association are not evidence of descendant survival or measured final affinity; no decoded final labels were observed in this role input.
A time derivative of a coordinate feature is not a spatial reward gradient and does not estimate an optimal guidance dose; no absolute coordinate target is asserted.
The registered dose recipes (W1/W2/W3) were not evaluated here; this handoff only supplies temporal coordinate evidence.
